!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = tissue: thyroid
!Sample_growth_protocol_ch1 = Our study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Peking University Third Hospital (LM2023126). Six patients, including 4 diagnosed with PTC in combination with Hashimoto thyroiditis and 2 diagnosed with Hashimoto thyroiditis were recruited in our study. All the patients signed the informed written consent for each subject and agreed to donate the specimens. For samples of adequate size, small fragments of each sample were snap frozen in optical cutting tissue (OCT) compound (Fisher Healthcare) and/or fixed in 10% formalin (Sigma-Aldrich).
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = The ST protocol was optimized for PTC and HT tissues according to manufacturer’s instructions (10x Genomics, CG000239 Rev E). The optimal incubation time for permeabilization was determined to be 22 min. Once optimal conditions were established, the cryosections (10 μm thick) per patient were cut onto the ST slides and processed immediately. Fixation, H&E staining, and imaging protocols were as describe by the manufacturer (10x Genomics, CG000239 Rev E). Sectioned slides were incubated at 37 ℃ for 1 min, fixed in 3.7% - 3.8% formaldehyde (Sigma-Aldrich) in PBS for 10 min, and then washed in 1x PBS (Medicago). For staining, sections were incubated in Mayer’s hematoxylin (Dako, Agilent) for 4 min, bluing buffer (Dako) for 30 sec, followed by eosin (Sigma-Aldrich) diluted 1:5 in Tris-base (0.45 M Tris, 0.5 M acetic acid, pH 6.0) for 30 sec. The slides were washed in water free of RNase and DNase after each of the staining steps. After air-drying, the slides were mounted with 85% glycerol (Merck Millipore) and coverslips. Bright-field images were taken at 20 × magnification using a Metafer Slide Scanning platform (MetaSystems). Raw images were stitched with VSlide software (MetaSystems). The coverslips and glycerol were removed after imaging by immersing slides in water free of RNase and DNase.
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = Library was performed according to the manufacter’s instructions (10x Genomics, CG000239 Rev E). After Reverse transcription, wells were washed with 0.1×SSC and incubated at 56 ℃ with interval shaking for 1.5 h with a tissue removal mix of Proteinase K (QIAGEN) and PKD buffer (QIAGEN, pH7.5) at a 1:1 ratio. The spatially barcoded cDNA was enzymatically released as previously described. Supernatants containing released cDNA were collected and transferred to 96-well plates for ST library preparation with an automated MBS 8000 system. Second-strand cDNA synthesis was followed by in vitro transcription, adaptor ligation, and a second RT. Sequencing handles and indexes were added in an indexing PCR, and the finished libraries were purified and quantified according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Visium spatial gene expression reagent kits, No. CG000239 Rev E). The libraries were sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq platform.
!Sample_description = 10x Visium
!Sample_data_processing = The demultiplexing, barcoded processing, gene counting and aggregation were made using the Space Ranger software v1.3.0 (https://support.10xgenomics.com/spatial-gene-expression/software/pipelines/latest/what-is-space-ranger)
!Sample_data_processing = R package Seurat (4.0.3) was used for downstream analysis such as normalization, integration, dimensionality reduction and clustering (https://satijalab.org/seurat/).
!Sample_data_processing = Assembly: GRCh38
